title: Rapid and blitz rules (and online differences)
summary: What changes in FIDE rapid and blitz, and how online play differs from over-the-board rules.

steps.md: FIDE time-control categories (KB rules.md): **standard** 60 minutes or more per player, **rapid** more than 10 and less than 60 minutes, **blitz** 10 minutes or less (increments count x60). Rapid and blitz are played under the Laws with Appendices A and B, which change some details; online play follows each platform's terms and the FIDE Online Chess Regulations.

steps.question: A game is played at 15 minutes + 10 seconds per move. Which category is it?
choices: Rapid: 15 + 60 x 10 s = 25 minutes, between 10 and 60
steps.explain: Count the increment times 60: 15 min + 10 s x 60 = 25 min, so rapid (App. A.1). 3+2 would be blitz (3 + 2 = 5 min).

steps.question: In rapid (App. A), must players record the moves?
choices: Not required: players need not keep score
Only in the last five minutes
steps.explain: Appendix A.2: players need not record the moves. (They lose some claim possibilities based on the scoresheet, so many arbiters recommend recording anyway.)

steps.question: In standard chess, the first completed illegal move gives the opponent two extra minutes. In rapid and blitz?
choices: One extra minute instead of two (App. A.3 / B.3); a second completed illegal move by the same player loses
The illegal move loses immediately in all cases
steps.explain: Rapid and blitz apply Article 7 with one minute instead of two. The second completed illegal move loses the game, unless the opponent cannot checkmate by any legal sequence (then it is a draw).

steps.question: An incorrect draw claim (threefold repetition) in a rapid game leads to...
choices: One minute added to the opponent's time, and the game continues
Two minutes added to your own time
steps.explain: Art. 9.5 with App. A.3: two minutes in standard become one minute in rapid/blitz, for the opponent. If the claim was based on a written intended move, that move must be played.

steps.question: Which of these is typical for **online** play but not for FIDE over-the-board rules?
choices: Premoves and automatic threefold/50-move draws, no touch-move
Pressing the clock with the same hand that moved
Flag fall counted as a draw when the opponent cannot mate
steps.explain: Online servers make many claims automatic and allow premoves; there is no touch-move. The other two items are OTB rules (Art. 6.2.3 and Art. 6.9); servers apply the insufficient-material rule automatically too.

steps.question: Your flag falls in a blitz game, but your opponent has only a king and a knight. What is the result under FIDE rules?
choices: Draw: the opponent cannot checkmate by any legal sequence of moves
steps.explain: Art. 6.9: flag fall loses unless the opponent cannot checkmate by any series of legal moves. K+N cannot force or even construct a mate against a bare king, so it is a draw. (With your own pawns on the board, a mate by K+N is possible and you would lose.)

steps.md: **Retrieval check.** Rapid: more than 10, less than 60 minutes; no scoresheet required; penalties of one minute instead of two. Blitz: 10 minutes or less. Online: platform rules, premoves, automatic claims, no touch-move.

sources: FIDE Laws of Chess (2023), Appendices A (Rapid) and B (Blitz)
